fact_sheet.business_description: The Company supplies routers and switches that carry Internet traffic and corporate data [D01]. It operates as an established infrastructure provider, utilizing an installed network, channel relationships, and a broad product line to support repeat purchases [D01].
products_customers_and_why_they_buy: Routers and switches sold to enterprise, service-provider, and smaller-business customers [D01]. Customers prioritize performance, compatibility, reliability, and support when standardizing networks [D06].
economics: Revenue grew 53% in the second quarter and 52% over the six-month period [D01]. Economics involve high levels of ongoing R&D and acquisitions to maintain product lines [D05]. Maintenance capex, owner-earnings inputs, and specific margins are not in pack [D02].
earnings_record: Fiscal second-quarter GAAP net income was $825 million ($0.23/share) compared to $282 million ($0.08/share) in the prior year [D01]. Six-month GAAP net income was $1.25 billion ($0.34/share) [D01]. Comparability is complicated by seven recent acquisitions and pooling accounting [D01].
competitive_position: Competitors include Lucent, Nortel, and Juniper [D06]. Moat evidence includes installed base, trained administrators, and compatibility advantages, though subject to technological substitution risks [D01, D06].
balance_sheet_and_capital_needs: Reported cash is mentioned but no specific figures for cash, debt, or leverage are provided [D02]. Acquisitions are used to fill product gaps [D01].
management_and_capital_allocation: Management describes increasing adoption of products by businesses and governments [D01]. Acquisitions are a primary capital allocation activity [D01]. Specific CEO tenure and incentive details are not in pack [D02].
price_and_valuation: Verified market price and P/E are not in pack [D02]. Second-quarter GAAP EPS of $0.23 annualizes to $0.92 per share pre-split; pro-forma EPS of $0.25 annualizes to $1.00 per share pre-split [D02].
what_the_market_is_worried_about: Rapid technological change and the necessity of constant engineering/acquisitions [D05]. Potential for capital-spending slowdowns [D05]. Impact of pooling restatements and share issuance on per-share earnings [D05]. Possibility of losing market share to competitors [D05].
recent_events: Two-for-one stock split announced February 8, 2000, with a February 22 record date and March 22 distribution [D01].
berkshire_context: Existing portfolio emphasizes consumer/financial franchises (e.g., Coca-Cola, American Express, Gillette); this opportunity would be assessed against existing capital and opportunity costs [D08].
missing_data: Current market price, P/E ratio, detailed balance sheet (debt/cash), maintenance capital expenditure requirements, and normalized owner earnings.

final.what_would_change_our_mind: A shift toward a stable, predictable business model with measurable owner earnings, where the competitive advantage is no longer dependent on constant R&D or external acquisitions.
final.memo:
We have spent time looking at this business, but it remains in our "too hard" pile. While the company occupies an important place in internet infrastructure, the rapid pace of technological change makes it impossible for us to determine if its competitive advantage will endure [D01, D05, D06].

True investment success requires us to understand how a business will look ten or twenty years from now [D08]. In this case, the company must rely on constant engineering and a steady stream of acquisitions just to stay relevant [D01, D05]. This creates a high risk of permanent capital loss that we are not willing to accept [D05].

Furthermore, the financial statements are obscured by the use of pooling accounting and frequent acquisitions, making it difficult to discern true owner earnings [D01]. Without a clear view of normalized earnings and maintenance capital needs, we cannot calculate a margin of safety [D02].

We prefer to allocate our capital to businesses with predictable, durable moats where we can be reasonably certain about the future [D08]. When the path is this uncertain, the only rational decision is to pass.
